cashflow.title: Decide this month's college-saving allocation
cashflow.why: Nothing is set aside for Liam and Josh and you must decide how college saving shares your cash flow.
steps: Pull the last three months of bank and credit statements
Use your reported net cash flow of $36,961/year to find monthly spare cash
Set a specific dollar amount to direct to college each month

cushion.title: Buy life insurance for both of you
cushion.why: The plan recommends using cash above your emergency reserve to close protection gaps, starting with life insurance for both of you.
steps: Gather current policy details and beneficiaries for each of you
Request term life quotes from your current agent for needed coverage
Pick one policy and set up the initial payment this month

college.title: Start a 529 with a set contribution
college.why: You have $0 in 529s and need about $113,509 more, roughly $4,609.22 more saved each year.
steps: Decide start contribution: $4,609.22 per year or monthly equivalent
Open a 529 account or access an existing 529 portal
Set an automatic contribution for the first transfer this month

investments.title: Schedule an invested-mix review with your advisor
investments.why: The plan suggests revisiting your invested mix so it matches both people's risk comfort and the cash you hold.
steps: Gather recent statements for IRAs, HSA, brokerage, and cash balances
Note the $150,000 cash and $210,000 invested savings amounts
Book a 30-minute meeting with your advisor this month
